{
  "threatModel": {
    "summary": "OnlineJudge is a Django API backend for accounts, problems, contests, submissions and administration. Production Docker startup initializes persistent state, starts Nginx on container ports 8000/1443, proxies APIs to Gunicorn on 127.0.0.1:8080, and runs Dramatiq workers. Submitted source is stored in PostgreSQL, queued through Redis and sent with problem limits and a shared-token header to separately deployed JudgeServers; the actual compiler/runtime sandbox is outside this repository. Development selects repository-local data and loopback database/cache services. Sources: README.md:24-33; Dockerfile:3-18; deploy/entrypoint.sh:58-77; deploy/supervisord.conf:19-46; deploy/nginx/nginx.conf:30-56; oj/settings.py:17-24; judge/dispatcher.py:125-184.",
    "assets": [
      "Account identity, password hashes, administrator/problem-management privileges, two-factor secrets, reset tokens, SSO tokens and OpenAPI keys reside in PostgreSQL-backed account records; production connection host defaults to oj-postgres:5432 while database/user/password come from POSTGRES_* environment variables; development uses 127.0.0.1:5435 and a repository-defined development database account. Secret values are referenced only. Sources: account/models.py:26-43; account/models.py:50-63; oj/production_settings.py:3-11; oj/dev_settings.py:6-14.",
      "Session state, submission throttling and pending judging tasks use Redis database 1; Dramatiq broker/results use database 4. Production defaults are redis://oj-redis:6379/1 and /4; development defaults are redis://127.0.0.1:6380/1 and /4. The connection builder supplies host/port without authentication or TLS options, so network isolation is a deployment prerequisite. Sources: oj/settings.py:193-239; oj/production_settings.py:14-17; oj/dev_settings.py:17-20; utils/cache.py:8-27; judge/dispatcher.py:23-31.",
      "The Django signing secret is read from /data/config/secret.key in production and <repository>/data/config/secret.key in development. Judge-server and SMTP credentials are separate PostgreSQL SysOptions values. Production initializes the signing file and overwrites the judge-server token from its environment during startup. Sources: oj/settings.py:23-24; oj/production_settings.py:23; oj/dev_settings.py:27; deploy/entrypoint.sh:8-10; deploy/entrypoint.sh:63; options/models.py:5-7; options/options.py:232-246.",
      "Private judging material includes test inputs, expected outputs, SPJ source, submission source and ranking integrity. Production test cases are /data/test_case/<test_case_id>/{1.in,1.out,...,info}; development uses <repository>/data/test_case/<test_case_id>. Archive downloads may additionally create <test_case_id>.zip in that directory or /tmp/<random>.zip. Sources: oj/settings.py:128; problem/views/admin.py:45-85; problem/views/admin.py:131-144; problem/views/admin.py:511-545; submission/models.py:25-41; judge/dispatcher.py:141-152.",
      "Published files are distinct from private test data: production avatar and upload consumers write /data/public/avatar/<generated-name> and /data/public/upload/<generated-name>; development writes the corresponding <repository>/data/public children. Nginx exposes /public using root /data. Generated account credentials are additionally written in cleartext to /tmp/<file_id>.xlsx for a super-administrator download and deleted on successful download. Sources: oj/settings.py:131-137; account/views/oj.py:74-87; utils/views.py:24-44; utils/views.py:60-75; deploy/nginx/locations.conf:1-3; account/views/admin.py:136-197.",
      "Deployment authority includes persistent TLS private key /data/ssl/server.key, root-capable initialization and process supervision, remotely downloaded frontend distribution contents, logs under /data/log, and conditional replicated test cases. Gunicorn runs as server:spj, Dramatiq as nobody, and the optional rsync daemon explicitly runs with uid/gid root. Sources: deploy/entrypoint.sh:20-24; deploy/entrypoint.sh:71-77; deploy/supervisord.conf:1-17; deploy/supervisord.conf:30-46; Dockerfile:14-16; deploy/test_case_rsync/rsyncd.conf:1-12."
    ],
    "trustBoundaries": [
      "Internet/browser HTTP input crosses Nginx into Django. Nginx proxies /api and enforces a 200M request-body limit. It sets X-Real-IP from remote_addr by default or from the configured LOWER_IP_HEADER; Django consumes that header as client identity and stores it in sessions, and contest submission CIDR enforcement consumes the stored value. Proxy-header trust therefore depends on deployment configuration and preventing unintended direct backend access. Sources: deploy/nginx/locations.conf:5-7; deploy/nginx/api_proxy.conf:1-4; deploy/entrypoint.sh:34-38; oj/settings.py:246; account/middleware.py:22-29; submission/views/oj.py:37-46.",
      "Browser sessions cross authentication and CSRF controls before application handlers. Middleware includes Django sessions, CSRF and authentication; login checks password, disabled state and configured TOTP. Selected upload/import/SSO/heartbeat APIs explicitly inherit CSRF exemption, so CSRF protection is interface-specific rather than universal. Sources: oj/settings.py:58-68; account/views/oj.py:155-179; utils/api/api.py:160-163; problem/views/admin.py:114-115; problem/views/admin.py:549-550; problem/views/admin.py:628; account/views/oj.py:421-436; conf/views.py:132.",
      "OpenAPI is a separate bearer-key authentication boundary: an APPKEY matching an enabled, non-disabled user sets request.user, marks CSRF processing complete and carries that user's existing role authority. A logged-in enabled user can regenerate its own key. This must be assessed independently of password/TOTP login. Sources: account/middleware.py:10-19; account/views/oj.py:409-418.",
      "Regular users, problem administrators, object owners and super-administrators have distinct application authority. Middleware gates /api/admin/ and /admin/ by administrator role; decorators enforce login, super-administrator and problem-management permissions; ensure_created_by enforces ownership or broader problem-management authority. Submission disclosure separately checks submitting user, privileged roles, problem ownership and sharing state. Sources: account/middleware.py:36-41; account/decorators.py:36-59; account/decorators.py:139-149; account/models.py:50-63; submission/models.py:43-52.",
      "Authenticated contestants cross contest visibility/password/time/rank controls and submission-specific IP restrictions before source submission. Submission source, chosen allowed language and problem identity are persisted and passed to judge_task. Per-user token-bucket throttling applies to session submissions; API-key submissions explicitly bypass that throttle. Sources: account/decorators.py:88-134; submission/views/oj.py:19-83.",
      "Administrator-controlled uploads cross ZIP/XML parsing and filesystem/publication boundaries. Test-case processing constructs numbered leaf names rather than extracting all archive paths, writes private test cases and info, and applies directory/file modes 0710/0640. ZIP and FPS imports create problem records; FPS images are written into the public upload directory. Problem RichTextField values are passed through XSSHtml on database preparation. Sources: problem/views/admin.py:34-111; problem/views/admin.py:549-625; problem/views/admin.py:672-705; fps/parser.py:12-32; fps/parser.py:109-120; problem/models.py:43-53; utils/models.py:7-10.",
      "Backend-to-JudgeServer is a separate service boundary carrying untrusted contestant source, administrator SPJ source, language/compiler configuration, limits and test-case identifiers. Backend hashes the stored shared token into X-Judge-Server-Token and POSTs to selected service URLs; external sandbox enforcement is not implemented here. SPJ compilation is separately reachable through the administrator API and calls compile_spj on a selected server. Sources: judge/dispatcher.py:55-88; judge/dispatcher.py:125-161; problem/views/admin.py:163-172; problem/urls/admin.py:7-16; README.md:28-29.",
      "JudgeServer registration is a reverse service boundary: the heartbeat API verifies the shared token's SHA-256 representation, then stores or updates hostname, service_url and server capacity. Dispatcher selection uses enabled, recent-heartbeat servers and task capacity. Consequently a valid judge credential grants registration/routing authority, not merely metrics submission. Sources: conf/views.py:132-161; conf/serializers.py:39-46; conf/models.py:18-23; judge/dispatcher.py:34-52; judge/dispatcher.py:84; judge/dispatcher.py:161.",
      "Redis-to-worker is an operational authority boundary. Redis database 4 supplies Dramatiq tasks executed as nobody; tasks subsequently access PostgreSQL, send email using stored SMTP credentials or dispatch judge requests. The same application settings load the signing secret and database/cache configuration for these workers. Sources: oj/settings.py:216-239; deploy/supervisord.conf:41-46; judge/tasks.py:9-14; account/tasks.py:10-22; oj/settings.py:17-24.",
      "Email crosses an external recipient boundary: super-administrators configure SMTP server/port/account/TLS; the email helper transmits account credentials to that configured server and sends password-reset links based on website_base_url to the account email address. Reset checks captcha, token equality and expiry before changing password and disabling TOTP. Sources: conf/views.py:33-73; utils/shortcuts.py:70-79; account/views/oj.py:280-329.",
      "Privileged startup/process control is separate from web authorization. Startup creates/chowns data, changes permissions and invokes Supervisor; Gunicorn drops to server:spj and workers use nobody. Supervisor exposes an HTTP control service only at 127.0.0.1:9005, with no authentication declaration in this configuration; actual accessibility depends on the surrounding container/network namespace. Sources: deploy/entrypoint.sh:58-77; deploy/supervisord.conf:10-17; deploy/supervisord.conf:30-46.",
      "Optional rsync replication crosses its own authenticated file-distribution boundary: master exposes TCP 873 on all host interfaces, exports /test_case read-only with chroot and an rsync secrets file, and mounts the master's test-case source read-only; slave writes its own /test_case and invokes rsync --delete using a password file. These host mappings are separate from the backend /data mount and cannot be assumed identical. Sources: deploy/test_case_rsync/docker-compose.yml:3-24; deploy/test_case_rsync/run.sh:3-32; deploy/test_case_rsync/rsyncd.conf:1-12.",
      "Build/publication trust includes an unpinned external frontend release: Docker build downloads latest OnlineJudgeFE dist.zip and extracts it into the application working directory, then Nginx serves that distribution. Production errors additionally cross an external telemetry boundary through the configured Raven/Sentry handler and fixed DSN reference. Sources: Dockerfile:5-16; deploy/nginx/locations.conf:9-20; oj/settings.py:140-182; oj/settings.py:242-244."
    ],
    "attackerCapabilities": [
      "User-provided review focus: authentication bypass, unintended remote code execution and server privilege escalation. These are requested investigation categories, not established vulnerabilities.",
      "An unauthenticated network client may call exposed public API routes, submit login/registration/reset/SSO inputs and provide arbitrary HTTP headers; registration requires enabled registration and captcha. No initial administrator, judge credential, database, Redis or host authority is assumed. Sources: oj/urls.py:3-16; account/urls/oj.py:12-30; account/views/oj.py:209-231; account/views/oj.py:280-329.",
      "A regular authenticated user can submit arbitrary source in a problem's allowed language for intended remote judging, upload an avatar and manage its account/session state; it does not thereby possess backend process or host authority. Sources: submission/views/oj.py:48-83; account/views/oj.py:64-87; account/views/oj.py:333-373.",
      "An OpenAPI-enabled user can possess and regenerate a bearer appkey that authenticates with that user's role and bypasses the session-submission token bucket. It is not assumed to know another user's appkey or to have an administrator role. Sources: account/views/oj.py:409-418; account/middleware.py:10-19; submission/views/oj.py:19-29.",
      "An administrator may supply problem archives, test-case ZIPs, editor files and SPJ code through administrative routes, but super-administrator configuration/user-management functions and object-ownership restrictions are distinct controls. Sources: oj/urls.py:5-16; problem/urls/admin.py:7-16; account/decorators.py:41-59; account/decorators.py:139-149; conf/views.py:33-58; account/views/admin.py:136-160.",
      "A holder of the judge-server shared credential can submit authenticated heartbeats including service_url and influence eligible judge destinations. Ordinary public clients are not assumed to possess that credential; acquisition or weak deployment provisioning would be an additional prerequisite. Sources: conf/views.py:132-161; judge/dispatcher.py:34-47; judge/dispatcher.py:55-64.",
      "A network peer with direct Redis, PostgreSQL, Supervisor or rsync reachability has materially different starting authority from a web-only attacker. Such access is not established by application source; optional rsync's host publish is explicitly configured while production backend/database/cache host exposure is absent from this repository. Sources: deploy/supervisord.conf:10-17; oj/production_settings.py:3-17; deploy/test_case_rsync/docker-compose.yml:13-14; README.md:31-33."
    ],
    "securityObjectives": [
      "Authenticate the correct user across password/TOTP, reset, session and OpenAPI interfaces, and prevent disabled accounts or lower-privilege actors from gaining another identity or administrator authority. Sources: account/views/oj.py:155-179; account/views/oj.py:313-329; account/middleware.py:10-19; account/decorators.py:22-50.",
      "Enforce administrator hierarchy, problem/contest ownership, contest participation restrictions and submission sharing rules before sensitive reads or writes. Sources: account/decorators.py:88-149; account/models.py:50-63; submission/models.py:43-52; submission/views/oj.py:37-46.",
      "Keep contestant/SPJ execution confined to the intended JudgeServer execution environment; backend source submission must not grant unintended backend or host execution, and sandbox claims require evidence from the external implementation. Sources: submission/views/oj.py:74-83; judge/dispatcher.py:69-88; judge/dispatcher.py:141-161; README.md:28-29.",
      "Keep private test cases, signing/judge/SMTP secrets and generated account credentials outside public file publication, authorized exports and intended recipients. Preserve /data/test_case permissions and explicit super-administrator/ownership checks on exports. Sources: deploy/entrypoint.sh:74-76; problem/views/admin.py:45-85; problem/views/admin.py:126-144; problem/views/admin.py:530-545; account/views/admin.py:136-197; deploy/nginx/locations.conf:1-3.",
      "Preserve judge routing and result integrity by accepting only authorized service registrations and binding dispatches to selected configured servers; preserve backend least privilege across startup, Gunicorn and asynchronous workers. Sources: conf/views.py:132-161; judge/dispatcher.py:34-64; judge/dispatcher.py:160-184; deploy/supervisord.conf:30-46.",
      "Apply limits at the actual shared consumers: Nginx API body limit, avatar 2MiB limit, allowed problem time/memory bounds, submission token bucket, judge-capacity selection and Dramatiq time/age limits. These controls differ by interface and do not establish blanket resource isolation. Sources: deploy/nginx/api_proxy.conf:4; account/views/oj.py:74-78; problem/serializers.py:55-58; submission/views/oj.py:19-29; judge/dispatcher.py:38-47; utils/shortcuts.py:86-87."
    ],
    "assumptions": [
      "Scope is the entire supplied current repository revision 3cae7f2830dceeb2727f8980bc65180e04edb47a (caller-provided context). This output is architecture mapping, not completed vulnerability-audit coverage; no application execution, service contact or attack input creation was performed.",
      "Production orchestration, host /data mount source, published backend ports, upstream proxy policy, database/cache network ACLs and actual environment values are not present in the inspected backend deployment. README delegates installation to another repository; host exposure and host privilege cannot be inferred from internal listeners. Sources: README.md:31-33; Dockerfile:18; deploy/nginx/nginx.conf:39-56; oj/production_settings.py:3-23.",
      "README describes a Seccomp Judger sandbox, but points to separate Judger/JudgeServer repositories; this repository forwards source, configuration and limits. Actual sandbox syscalls, process uid/capabilities, mounts and escape resistance are unresolved external controls. Sources: README.md:28-29; judge/dispatcher.py:141-161.",
      "FORCE_HTTPS selects the redirect configuration, but that configuration explicitly keeps /api/judge_server_heartbeat proxied over HTTP. TLS terminates on container port 1443 with /data/ssl/server.{crt,key}, while HTTP redirect targets the ordinary https host URL; external port mapping/proxy behavior must be supplied. Sources: deploy/entrypoint.sh:20-32; deploy/nginx/https_redirect.conf:1-6; deploy/nginx/nginx.conf:46-56.",
      "The lazy judge-token default uses JUDGE_SERVER_TOKEN or a generated random value, but production entrypoint explicitly assigns SysOptions.judge_server_token from the environment string. An unset/empty environment therefore must not be modeled as automatically retaining the random fallback. Actual provisioning is unknown. Sources: options/options.py:90-92; options/options.py:116; options/options.py:128-147; deploy/entrypoint.sh:63.",
      "Production and development bootstrap scripts use repository-defined initial super-administrator credential arguments; the management command skips creation when user id 1 exists. Actual first-start exposure and subsequent password replacement are unknown; credential literals are intentionally omitted. Sources: deploy/entrypoint.sh:61-62; init_db.sh:14-18; utils/management/commands/inituser.py:22-31.",
      "README runtime badges describe older Python/Django versions than the Dockerfile and pinned requirements actually consume. For architecture/runtime analysis use Docker Python 3.7 Alpine and requirements Django 2.1.7, rather than README badges. Sources: README.md:3-5; Dockerfile:1; deploy/requirements.txt:4.",
      "Native Windows production deployment is not established. Container scripts require Unix shell, POSIX users/modes, /data and /tmp; development DATA_DIR derives from the repository but several export consumers still hard-code /tmp. Windows filesystem/access semantics therefore require separate evidence if that deployment is intended. Sources: deploy/entrypoint.sh:1-6; deploy/entrypoint.sh:71-77; oj/dev_settings.py:27; account/views/admin.py:147; problem/views/admin.py:538.",
      "Optional rsync compose has differing image names for master and slave and supplies no RSYNC_MASTER_ADDR to the slave, although the slave runner consumes it. The master's $PWD/data/backend/test_case and slave's $PWD/test_case do not themselves prove correspondence with the backend's /data/test_case. Sources: deploy/test_case_rsync/docker-compose.yml:3-24; deploy/test_case_rsync/run.sh:7; oj/settings.py:128; oj/production_settings.py:23.",
      "Frontend implementation is not checked into this source inventory and Docker retrieves its latest release without a pinned digest here; actual archive layout, frontend rendering and published browser behavior require the fetched artifact or separately authorized frontend source. Sources: Dockerfile:14-16; README.md:26-29; deploy/nginx/locations.conf:9-20."
    ]
  },
